# Method-owned dependency formals

The independently authored nongeneric SDK interface keeps `<M extends Mark>`
on an abstract requirement and a default that invokes it. Original input
providers use alpha-equivalent `<N extends Mark>` scopes. The dependency JAR
and immutable harness remain unchanged during recovery and recompilation.

The profile extends the original raw-parameter fixture and retains every
original class/member attribute, complete Signature and runtime descriptor.
It compares 252 additional identities, 90 state observations and 30 ordered
failures through direct, interface, reflected, inherited-default and independent
subclass routes. Mutable aliases, captured nulls and effects before exceptions
must match. It adds no input bridge or inherited implementation.

A same-Code mutation replaces the invariant method-owned parameter argument
with a literal `Mark`. Recovery and independent javac must reject it even
though the runtime method descriptors remain unchanged. Native negatives also
cover result/formal/visibility/static/throws drift and missing class arguments.

`--raw-dependency-defaults` adds an unused SDK class formal and inherits its
original default through a raw interface. The input methods retain their own
independent generic declarations and never override that default. Complete
original SDK and input metadata, 24 additional identities, 24 state observations
and six SDK cast failures must match. Renaming an input generic method into
that raw default slot keeps Code and descriptors but fails both recovery and
javac. Native coverage also rejects an inherited generic class provider for
the same raw slot and retains unchanged defaults without copying methods.
The original typed-parameter negatives still fail in this raw default profile.
Native coverage retains a class-owned covariant result so that the source
subsignature check cannot accidentally erase or reject result metadata.
